mainTopic: Vows of offerings: forgotten or unclear vows, the value of a vowed animal, רבי's view on bringing a bigger animal, and the six boxes for נדבה money
overview: The amud opens with the end of a משנה about vows of offerings. If the person forgot exactly which animal he named, he must bring every animal that could match, and sometimes birds too. If he named no animal at all, a lamb is enough. Next, the משנה sets prices for vowed animals. If he names only the animal, the price includes its נסכים. If he names the price himself, the animal alone must be worth it, and two cheaper animals or a different color do not count. The תנא קמא and רבי argue over whether a bigger animal can replace a smaller one he promised. The גמרא explains that the lamb-or-bird argument depends on local speech, and it brings a ברייתא about vowing an עולה worth a סלע. It then shows that the bull-and-calf ruling follows רבי, so the משנה mixes his view with that of רבנן. Finally, the גמרא asks why the מקדש had six boxes for נדבה money and records several answers. בר פדא's answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Adding a turtledove and a young pigeon to the list
steps.stepSummary: The ruling from just before ends by adding a תור and a בן יונה to the list of animals the person must bring.
steps.simpleTranslation: He adds to them a turtledove and a young pigeon.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is finishing a ruling that started just before this point. To the long list of animals he must bring, he also adds two birds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When someone is unsure which offering he promised, he brings every possible option so that one of them is surely the right one. Birds can also be brought as this kind of offering, so the list is not complete until a תור and a בן יונה are added.

keyTerms.meaning: adds on
turtledove, a bird used for offerings
young pigeon, a bird used for offerings

phrases.english: He adds to them a turtledove and a young pigeon.

steps.triggerLanguage: מוֹסִיף עֲלֵיהֶן תּוֹר וּבֶן יוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the list from the case just before this point
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the earlier uncertain case, he also brings a turtledove and a young pigeon.

steps.title: Vowing a thanks offering or peace offering without naming an animal
steps.stepSummary: If someone vows a תודה or שלמים without naming an animal, a כבש is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone says, 'I take upon myself a thanks offering and a peace offering,' he brings a lamb.
steps.whatsHappening: A new rule begins. If a person promises a תודה or שלמים and doesn't say which animal, he can bring a lamb.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a vow is unclear, we hold the person only to the smallest thing his words could mean. A lamb is the cheapest animal used for these offerings, so it fulfills his promise. Birds are not mentioned here because these offerings come only from animals.

keyTerms.meaning: 'I take upon myself,' the wording of a vow (נדר)
thanks offering
peace offering
lamb

phrases.english: 'I take upon myself a thanks offering and a peace offering'
– he brings a lamb.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵי עָלַי תּוֹדָה וּשְׁלָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the earlier list to vows of תודה and שלמים
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An open-ended vow of a תודה or שלמים is fulfilled with a lamb.

steps.title: He named a type of animal but forgot which one
steps.stepSummary: If he named cattle, or animals in general, but forgot which one, he must bring every possibility, both males and females.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he says, 'I specified from cattle and I don't know what I specified,' he brings a bull and a cow, a male calf and a female calf. If he says, 'From animals, and I don't know what I specified,' he brings a bull and a cow, a male calf and a female calf, a ram and a ewe, a grown male goat and a grown female goat, a young male goat and a young female goat, a male lamb and a female lamb.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now covers someone who did name a specific animal but forgot which one. He has to bring every animal that fits the group he remembers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the vow was specific, so a lamb is no longer enough. The animal he actually named might have been bigger, so he brings every possibility. Both males and females are included because a שלמים can be male or female. If he only remembers 'cattle,' the options are bulls and calves. If he only remembers 'animals,' the list grows to include sheep and goats of every age and both sexes.

keyTerms.meaning: I specified, meaning I named the exact animal
cattle (bulls, cows, calves)
domestic animal (cattle, sheep, goats)
grown male goat
young goat, a kid
young lamb

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with step 2. In step 2 he never named an animal, so the smallest one is enough. Here he did name one and forgot it, so he must cover every possibility.

phrases.english: 'I specified from cattle,'
'and I don't know what I specified'
– he brings a bull and a cow, a male calf and a female calf.
'From animals, and I don't know what I specified'
– he brings a bull and a cow, a male calf and a female calf,
a ram and a ewe, a grown male goat and a grown female goat,
a young male goat and a young female goat, a male lamb and a female lamb.

steps.triggerLanguage: פֵּירַשְׁתִּי מִן בָּקָר, וְאֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ מָה פֵּירַשְׁתִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the case where a specific animal was named and then forgotten
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When he forgets which animal he named, he brings every animal that could match, both male and female.

steps.title: Vowing an animal without naming a price
steps.stepSummary: If he only names the animal, the set amount of money covers the animal together with its נסכים.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he says, 'I take upon myself a bull,' he brings it and its libations for a מנה. For 'a calf,' he brings it and its libations for five. For 'a ram,' he brings it and its libations for two. For 'a lamb,' he brings it and its libations for a סלע.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins: how expensive the promised animal has to be. Each animal gets a minimum value, and that value includes its נסכים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person did not mention a price, so the standard amount covers everything: the animal, its flour offering, and its wine. The amounts are a מנה (100 דינרים) for a bull, five סלעים for a calf, two סלעים for a ram, and one סלע for a lamb.

keyTerms.meaning: its נסכים: the flour offering and wine poured that go with the animal
a coin value equal to 100 דינרים
a coin worth 4 דינרים
calf
ram

phrases.english: 'I take upon myself a bull'
– he brings it and its libations for a מנה,
'A calf' – he brings it and its libations for five,
phrases.notes: "Five" means five סלעים. The coin word is left out but understood.

phrases.english: 'A ram' – he brings it and its libations for two,
'A lamb' – he brings it and its libations for a סלע.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵי עָלַי שׁוֹר יָבִיא הוּא וּנְסָכָיו בְּמָנֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from unclear vows to the value of a vowed animal
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When only the animal is named, the standard value includes its נסכים.

steps.title: Vowing an animal with a named price
steps.stepSummary: If he names the price along with the animal, the animal alone must be worth that amount, and the נסכים are paid for on top of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'A bull for a מנה': he brings one for a מנה, not counting its libations. 'A calf for five': he brings one for five, not counting its libations. 'A ram for two': he brings one for two, not counting its libations. 'A lamb for a סלע': he brings one for a סלע, not counting its libations.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the opposite of the last step. When the person names a price himself, that price covers only the animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By stating the price as part of the vow, he tied that amount to the animal itself. So the animal must be worth the full amount, and the נסכים are an extra cost. The amounts are the same as in step 4. The only thing that changes is whether the נסכים are included.

keyTerms.meaning: not counting its נסכים; they are an extra cost

steps.whatToRemember: Naming just the animal means the standard price covers the animal and its נסכים together. Naming the price yourself means the animal alone must be worth that price, and the נסכים come on top.

phrases.english: 'A bull for a מנה' – he brings one for a מנה,
not counting its libations.
'A calf for five' – he brings one for five,
not counting its libations.
'A ram for two' – he brings one for two,
not counting its libations.
'A lamb for a סלע' – he brings one for a סלע,
not counting its libations.

steps.triggerLanguage: שׁוֹר בְּמָנֶה יָבִיא בְּמָנֶה חוּץ מִנְּסָכָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with step 4: naming the price leaves the נסכים out of that amount
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the vow names a price, the animal alone must be worth that price, and the נסכים are extra.

steps.title: Two cheaper bulls cannot replace one bull worth a מנה
steps.stepSummary: If he vowed a bull worth a מנה and brought two bulls that together are worth a מנה, he has not fulfilled his vow, even if each one is worth almost a מנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said 'a bull for a מנה' and brought two bulls for a מנה together, he has not fulfilled his vow. This is true even if each one is worth a מנה minus one דינר.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its list of price vows. He promised one bull at a set price, and two cheaper bulls do not count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 taught that when he names a price, the animal itself must be worth that price. So two animals that add up to the price, or are each almost at the price, are not the one animal he promised. Being worth almost a מנה is still not a מנה.

keyTerms.meaning: A sum of money equal to one hundred דינרים
A coin; one hundred of them make a מנה
He has not fulfilled his obligation

phrases.english: If he said: 'A bull for a maneh,'
phrases.notes: A מנה is one hundred דינרים. He is promising one bull worth that much.

phrases.english: and he brought two bulls for a maneh together
he has not fulfilled his obligation,
and even if this one is worth a maneh less one dinar
and that one is worth a maneh less one dinar.

steps.triggerLanguage: שׁוֹר בְּמָנֶה וְהֵבִיא שְׁנַיִם בְּמָנֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the rule from step 5 (the animal itself must be worth the price) to a case of two cheaper animals.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One animal at a named price cannot be replaced by two cheaper animals, even if each is just one דינר short.

steps.title: Bringing a different color or size than he promised
steps.stepSummary: A different color, or a smaller animal than promised, does not count. If he promised a small one and brought a big one, the תנא קמא says it counts and רבי says it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said 'black' and brought white, or 'white' and brought black, or 'big' and brought small, he has not fulfilled his vow. If he said 'small' and brought big, he has fulfilled it. רבי says: he has not fulfilled it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves from vows with a price to vows with a description (color or size) and lists which changes are allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Changing the color or bringing less than he promised breaks the vow. Bringing a bigger animal is the argument: the תנא קמא sees the small one as included inside the big one. רבי holds he must bring exactly what he said.

keyTerms.meaning: Black
White
Big / small
He has fulfilled his obligation

steps.confusionAlert: רבי's opinion is only about the last case (promised small, brought big). Everyone agrees about the earlier cases.

phrases.english: If he said 'black' and brought white,
or 'white' and brought black,
or 'big' and brought small, he has not fulfilled his obligation.
If he said 'small' and brought big, he has fulfilled his obligation.
רבי says: He has not fulfilled his obligation.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁחוֹר וְהֵבִיא לָבָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from price vows to vows with a description of color or size.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A changed color or a smaller animal never counts. A bigger animal than promised counts according to the תנא קמא but not according to רבי.
steps.whatToRemember: The end of the משנה: a vow with a named price or description must be kept exactly. The only argument is over bringing a bigger animal.

steps.title: The lamb-or-bird argument depends on local speech
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the תנא קמא (who says a lamb) and רבי אלעזר בן עזריה (who allows a bird) do not truly argue; each follows how people in his place used the word עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: They do not really disagree. Each Sage ruled according to the way people speak in his own place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by going back to the earlier part of the משנה about a plain vow of an עולה, and shows that the two opinions there are not a real argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It looked like a disagreement about the law: lamb only, or a bird too. The גמרא says the law is the same for both; a vow means what people in that place mean by the word. In one place 'עולה' meant an animal, and in the other it could also mean a bird.

keyTerms.meaning: And they do not disagree
Each Sage according to his own place (its local custom and speech)
A burnt offering, burned completely on the מזבח

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a key rule about vows: words are understood the way people speak in that place. This is why the ruling can change from place to place.

phrases.english: GEMARA
And they do not disagree,
phrases.notes: "They" are the תנא קמא and רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, from the earlier part of the משנה about vowing a plain עולה.

phrases.english: this Sage ruled according to his place,
and that Sage ruled according to his place.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא פְּלִיגִי מָר כִּי אַתְרֵיהּ וּמָר כִּי אַתְרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back from the end of the משנה to its earlier dispute about vowing a plain עולה (lamb or bird).
steps.terutzResolutionType: Turns an apparent argument about the law into a difference in local speech
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two תנאים argue about the law of a plain vow of an עולה.
steps.terutzMaskana: They agree on the law; each one follows what the word עולה means where he lives.

steps.title: An עולה for a סלע means a lamb
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that one who vows an עולה worth a סלע must bring a lamb, since only a lamb is offered at that price.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: One who says 'I take upon myself an עולה for a סלע for the מזבח' must bring a lamb, because the only thing offered on the מזבח at the price of a סלע is a lamb.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about a vow where he names a price but not the animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The price tells us which animal he meant. Since only a lamb costs a סלע, the vow is understood as a lamb.

keyTerms.meaning: A coin; here, the price he named for the קרבן
A lamb
'It is upon me' — the wording of a vow (נדר)

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
'It is upon me to bring a burnt offering for a sela for the altar,'
he must bring a lamb,
for you have nothing that is offered for a sela
on the altar except a lamb.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן הֲרֵי עָלַי עוֹלָה בְּסֶלַע לַמִּזְבֵּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a ברייתא about vows that name a price, continuing the topic of what a vow is understood to mean.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vow of an עולה 'for a סלע' means a lamb, since that is the only offering at that price.

steps.title: He named something worth a סלע but forgot what
steps.stepSummary: If he says he specified a particular animal offered for a סלע but forgot which, he must bring every kind of animal offered for a סלע.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he says: 'I specified something offered for a סלע, but I don't know what I specified,' he must bring one of everything that is offered on the מזבח for a סלע.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with a case where he says he named a specific animal but forgot which one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 9 the price alone pointed to a lamb. Here he says he named something specific, so we can't be sure it was a lamb. Like step 3, when he forgot, he must bring every possibility.

keyTerms.meaning: I specified (I named it clearly)
I do not know
Of every kind

steps.whatToRemember: A plain price of a סלע means a lamb. If he specified something and forgot what, he must bring every animal at that price to be safe.

phrases.english: 'I specified something that is offered for a sela,'
but I do not know what I specified,'
he must bring one of every kind that is offered for a sela
on the altar.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁקָּרֵב בְּסֶלַע פֵּירַשְׁתִּי וְאֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ מָה פֵּירַשְׁתִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same ברייתא; moves from a plain price vow to a case where he named something specific and forgot it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If he named a specific offering at the price of a סלע and forgot which, he brings every offering that costs a סלע.

steps.title: Why bring both a bull and a calf?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says that one who specified cattle but forgot which kind must bring a פר and an עגל. The גמרא asks why one bull is not enough either way.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: if he says, 'I specified an animal from the herd, but I don't know which one I specified,' he must bring a bull and a calf. The גמרא asks: Why? Let him just bring a bull, since that works either way!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה and challenges it. A bull alone should satisfy any possible vow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he really vowed a bull, the bull fulfills it. If he vowed a calf, a bull is bigger and worth more, so the calf should be included in it. So the requirement to bring both animals looks unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: I specified; I named exactly which animal
A bull, a fully grown animal
A calf, a young animal from the herd
Whichever way you look at it; covers every possibility

phrases.english: "I specified an animal from the herd,
but I do not know what I specified"
he must bring a bull and a calf.
Why?
Let him bring a bull, whichever way you look at it!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמַּאי? וְלַיְתֵי פַּר, מִמָּה נַפְשָׁךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the forgotten-animal case for a סלע to the parallel case of cattle, and challenges the משנה's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that he must bring both a פר and an עגל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A bull satisfies a vow for a bull and also includes a calf, so one bull should cover every possibility.

steps.title: This follows רבי: bigger does not count
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that this ruling follows רבי, who holds that one who promised a small animal and brought a large one has not fulfilled his vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion is this? It is רבי, who said: if he promised a small one and brought a large one, he has not fulfilled his vow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by assigning this ruling to רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי, the animal must match exactly what was promised, and a bigger one does not count. So if he had vowed a calf, a bull would not fulfill it, and he must bring both to be safe.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose opinion is this? (a question asking which תנא a ruling follows)
He has not fulfilled his obligation

phrases.english: Whose opinion is this? It is Rabbi,
who said: if he promised a small one and brought a large one,
he has not fulfilled his obligation.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא מַנִּי? רַבִּי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the ruling to a specific תנא (רבי).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A bull should cover a calf, so one animal is enough.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי, a larger animal does not fulfill a vow for a smaller one, so he must bring both.

steps.title: But the end of the משנה lists רבי as the one who disagrees
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer. The end of the same משנה gives the ruling that a big animal counts and then quotes רבי as disagreeing, so the main voice of the משנה seems not to be רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the משנה follows רבי, look at the end of it: 'A bull worth a מנה' and he brought two worth a מנה together: he has not fulfilled his vow, even if each is worth a מנה minus a דינר. 'A black one' and he brought a white one, 'a white one' and he brought a black one, 'a large one' and he brought a small one: he has not fulfilled it. 'A small one' and he brought a large one: he has fulfilled it. רבי says: he has not fulfilled it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks its own answer by quoting the end of the משנה (the same text from steps 6–7), now used as evidence against the claim that the משנה follows רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the end of the משנה, the anonymous voice says that small-promised, large-brought counts, and רבי is quoted separately as disagreeing. That shows the main anonymous voice of this משנה is not רבי. So how can the earlier line about the bull and calf follow רבי? Step 14 spells out the problem, and step 15 answers it.

keyTerms.meaning: Say the end of the משנה; look at the later clause
Missing one דינר; just under the full value

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not asking about the cases of the bull worth a מנה or the colors. It quotes them only to reach the final line, where רבי appears as the one who disagrees.

phrases.english: If it is Rabbi, say the latter clause:
"A bull worth a maneh" and he brought two worth a maneh together,
he has not fulfilled his obligation,
and even if this one is worth a maneh less a dinar
and that one is worth a maneh less a dinar.
"A black one" and he brought a white one,
"A white one" and he brought a black one,
"A large one" and he brought a small one: he has not fulfilled his obligation,
"A small one" and he brought a large one: he has fulfilled his obligation,
Rabbi says: he has not fulfilled his obligation.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי רַבִּי, אֵימָא סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 12 by reading the end of the same משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the bull-and-calf ruling follows רבי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The end of the משנה presents רבי as a dissenter against the anonymous ruling, which shows that the anonymous author of the משנה is not רבי. So assigning the earlier anonymous line to רבי creates an inconsistent משנה.

steps.title: The mixed-up משנה problem
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out the end of its challenge. If the first clause follows רבי, then the first and last clauses follow רבי while the middle clause follows רבנן, which seems very odd.
steps.simpleTranslation: So the first clause and the last clause would follow רבי, and the middle clause would follow רבנן?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the challenge from the last step. It points out how strange the משנה would look if we accept the answer that the first clause follows רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 said the bull-and-calf ruling follows רבי. Step 13 noted that the main voice in the end of the משנה is not רבי. Put together, the משנה would jump from רבי to רבנן and back to רבי, and normally we do not expect a משנה to switch opinions like that.

keyTerms.meaning: The first clause of a משנה or ברייתא
The last clause
The middle clause
The Sages, the majority view that argues with a single named sage

phrases.english: The first clause and the last clause follow Rabbi,
phrases.notes: The last clause is where רבי is quoted by name; the first clause is the bull-and-calf ruling from step 12.

phrases.english: and the middle clause follows the Rabbis?!

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישָׁא וְסֵיפָא – רַבִּי, וּמְצִיעֲתָא – רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge begun in step 13 by stating its full consequence.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in step 12 that the bull-and-calf ruling follows רבי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the first clause follows רבי while the middle clause follows רבנן and the end quotes רבי, the משנה switches opinions twice, which is very unlikely.

steps.title: Yes, and the משנה is pointing to a dispute
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the odd split. The first and last clauses follow רבי and the middle follows רבנן. The משנה is telling us that this matter is a מחלוקת between רבי and רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, the first and last clauses follow רבי and the middle follows רבנן. This is what the משנה means: this matter is a dispute between רבי and רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the split is real. It explains that the משנה is not one single voice here; it is showing us an argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of avoiding the split, the גמרא accepts it. The final line, where רבי is named, is read as the משנה's way of saying that the earlier rulings depend on a מחלוקת. So the bull-and-calf ruling stands as רבי's view, and the challenge is resolved.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes
And this is what it means, used to reread a text
A dispute between sages

steps.whatToRemember: The bull-and-calf ruling follows רבי, who holds that bringing a bigger animal does not fulfill a vow for a smaller one. The משנה contains both views and is pointing out the dispute.

phrases.english: Yes, the first and last clauses follow Rabbi,
the middle clause follows the Rabbis,
and this is what it is saying:
this matter is a dispute between Rabbi and the Rabbis.
phrases.notes: "This matter" is the bull-and-calf ruling. The משנה is showing that not everyone agrees with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין, רֵישָׁא וְסֵיפָא רַבִּי, מְצִיעֲתָא רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 14 by accepting the split and rereading the משנה as presenting a dispute.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepts the challenge's premise and reinterprets the משנה's structure.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A משנה would not switch between רבי and רבנן clause by clause, so the first clause cannot follow רבי.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה does switch, and its closing line signals that the matter is a מחלוקת between רבי and רבנן.

steps.title: What did the six donation boxes stand for?
steps.stepSummary: A new topic opens. The גמרא quotes a משנה saying there were six boxes for נדבה money and asks what they corresponded to. It gives a memory aid for the sages who will answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there: six boxes were for gift offerings. What did they correspond to? (A memory aid for the names of the answering sages.)
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new discussion. It quotes a משנה about six collection boxes and asks what the number six stands for. This sets up the answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Other boxes in the מקדש had clear purposes, but six boxes all for נדבה seems like more than needed. The גמרא wants to know the reason for this number. The סימן tells us several sages will answer, one after another.

keyTerms.meaning: There, meaning in another place or tractate
A voluntary gift offering
What does it correspond to?
A memory aid, usually letters standing for names or ideas

phrases.english: We learned there:
phrases.notes: "There" is a משנה in שקלים, about the collection boxes in the מקדש.

phrases.english: six were for gift offerings,
To what do they correspond?
(A memory aid: the letters for the answering sages.)
phrases.notes: Some versions have the letters in round brackets, but the corrected wording swaps them for the letters in square brackets. Either way, they help you remember the sages who answer.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן הָתָם: שִׁשָּׁה לִנְדָבָה, כְּנֶגֶד מִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic, after the bull-and-calf discussion is resolved.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason there were six boxes for נדבה, and what they correspond to.

steps.title: חזקיה: six boxes for six families of כהנים
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה says the six boxes match the six family groups of כהנים serving each week. The חכמים set it up this way so the families would stay at peace with each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיה said: They correspond to the six family groups of the כהנים. The חכמים set this up for them so there would be peace between them.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the first answer to the question about the six boxes. חזקיה ties each box to one family group of כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each weekly shift of כהנים was split into family groups called בתי אבות. Giving each family its own box kept their offerings separate. That way they would not come to fight, which is why the חכמים set it up this way.

keyTerms.meaning: Family groups of כהנים, each serving on its own day within the weekly shift
Priests who served in the מקדש
They set up, as an enactment
Peace, here meaning no quarrels

phrases.english: Ḥizkiyya said:
They correspond to the six family groups of the priests,
which the Sages set up for them
so that there would be peace between one another.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר חִזְקִיָּה: כְּנֶגֶד שִׁשָּׁה בָּתֵּי אָבוֹת הַכֹּהֲנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to the question in step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The six boxes match the six בתי אבות of כהנים, so each family has its own box and they stay at peace.

steps.title: Many boxes so the coins would not rot
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says there was so much נדבה money that the חכמים set up many boxes, so the coins would not rot at the bottom of one overfilled box.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says: Since there was so much נדבה money, they set up many boxes for it, so that the coins would not rot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer to the question of why there were six boxes. רבי יוחנן says the reason was practical, not symbolic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חזקיה connected the six boxes to six groups of people (the כהנים families). רבי יוחנן does not tie the number to anything. There was simply a lot of money, and spreading it over many boxes kept the coins from sitting too long and going bad.

keyTerms.meaning: Collection boxes in the בית המקדש, shaped like a horn: narrow on top, wide on the bottom
Voluntary gift money, used to buy extra offerings
Plentiful / many
Would rot or decay
Coins, money

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says:
Since the gift money was plentiful,
they set up many collection boxes for them,
so that the coins would not rot.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: מִתּוֹךְ שֶׁהַנְּדָבָה מְרוּבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the question in step 16, different from חזקיה's answer in step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What did the six boxes for נדבה money correspond to?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They do not stand for anything. There was a lot of money, and many boxes kept the coins from rotting.

steps.title: Six boxes for six kinds of animals, following רבי
steps.stepSummary: זעירי says the six boxes match six kinds of animals: bull, calf, ram, lamb, young goat and grown goat. He explains this fits רבי, who holds that if you promised a small animal and brought a big one, you have not kept your promise.
steps.simpleTranslation: זעירי says: The boxes match a bull and a calf, a ram and a lamb, a young goat and a grown goat. This follows רבי, who says: if someone promised a small animal and brought a big one, he has not fulfilled his promise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third answer. זעירי says each box was for a different kind of animal, and he names the תנא whose view makes this necessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Six separate boxes only make sense if the small and big versions of each animal must be kept apart. According to רבי, a big animal does not count for someone who promised a small one, so the money for each size needs its own box. That is why זעירי says this explanation follows רבי.

keyTerms.meaning: Corresponding to, matching
A grown bull and a young calf
A grown ram and a young lamb
A young goat and a grown goat
He has not fulfilled his obligation

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the sizes. In each pair, one animal is the young or small version and the other is the grown or big version of the same species. That is the whole reason the pairs are kept apart.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ties back to the מחלוקת between רבי and רבנן from steps 13-15. Only רבי's view needs separate boxes for small and big animals.

phrases.english: And Zeiri says:
They correspond to a bull and a calf,
a ram and a lamb,
a young goat and a grown goat.
And this follows Rabbi,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר: קָטָן וְהֵבִיא גָּדוֹל – לֹא יָצָא.
phrases.english: who says: if he promised a small one and brought a big one, he has not fulfilled his obligation.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּזְעֵירִי אָמַר: כְּנֶגֶד פַּר וָעֵגֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another answer to the question in step 16. It also links back to the opinion of רבי from steps 13-15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What did the six boxes for נדבה money correspond to?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Six kinds of animals, a small and a big version of each species. This fits רבי's view that a big animal does not count for a promised small one.

steps.title: בר פדא begins his answer: bulls and rams
steps.stepSummary: בר פדא starts a fourth answer: the boxes match certain kinds of animals, beginning with bulls and rams. His list continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: בר פדא says: The boxes match the bulls, and the rams...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a fourth answer from בר פדא. Only the start of his list appears here; the rest continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like זעירי, בר פדא links the boxes to kinds of animals. His list is a different one: it starts with "the bulls" and "the rams" as whole groups rather than small-and-big pairs. Wait for the rest of his list before drawing conclusions.

keyTerms.meaning: The bulls
The rams

phrases.english: And bar Padda says:
They correspond to the bulls, and the rams,

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבַר פְּדָא אָמַר: כְּנֶגֶד הַפָּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A fourth answer to the question in step 16. It continues on the next amud.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What did the six boxes for נדבה money correspond to?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Certain groups of animals, starting with bulls and rams. The list continues on the next amud.
